subject: Archaeology
title: Mummification: The Science of Eternity
description: A 60-second lesson on Mummification: The Science of Eternity.

hook.text: Egyptians believed that if the body decayed, the soul was destroyed forever. Preservation was survival.

buildup.text: Embalmers removed the brain through the nose with a hook and stored organs in four canopic jars.

discovery.text: The body was packed in natron salt for 40 days, dehydrating it completely before wrapping in linen.

twist.text: Full mummification was only for the rich. Poor Egyptians were buried in sand, which preserved them naturally.

climax.text: CT scans of mummies reveal heart disease, dental infections, and even cancer — ancient bodies tell modern stories.

punchline.text: The quest for eternal life gave modern medicine ancient patients.

quiz.question: What was the purpose of natron salt in mummification?
options: It killed bacteria to prevent infection during the process
It dehydrated the body completely over 40 days
It gave the skin a golden color for the afterlife

details.summary: Egyptian mummification preserved bodies through organ removal, natron desiccation, and resin-soaked linen wrapping over a seventy-day process. The Egyptians believed preserving the body was essential for the soul's survival in the afterlife.
details.whyItMatters: Mummification reveals sophisticated chemical knowledge thousands of years before modern chemistry. Studying mummies provides medical data about ancient diseases, diets, and living conditions unavailable from any other source.
takeaways: The process took about seventy days from death to burial
Organs were removed and the body dried with natron salt
Body preservation was believed essential for afterlife survival

faq.question: What was natron and how did it preserve bodies?
faq.answer: Natron is a natural salt mixture found in Egyptian lake beds. Packed around the body for forty days, it absorbed moisture and fat, preventing bacterial decomposition. The result was a dried, preserved body that could last thousands of years in arid conditions.

faq.question: Why were organs removed during mummification?
faq.answer: Internal organs decay rapidly, so embalmers removed the lungs, liver, stomach, and intestines through an abdominal incision. These were preserved separately in canopic jars. The brain was extracted through the nose and discarded as unimportant.
